question.text: What is the primary advantage of buying options for hedging compared to using futures?

answer.text: Options limit the downside risk while preserving the upside potential
Options are always cheaper than futures
Options provide perfect hedges while futures don't
Options have no margin requirements while futures do

explanation.text: The Logic: Buying options limits the buyer's loss to the premium paid while leaving the upside open. Futures and forwards, in contrast, lock in the exposure without the same one-sided protection. The Trap: Options are not necessarily cheaper than futures and do not by themselves remove margin requirements for sellers; their advantage is the asymmetric payoff for the buyer. Note: Pages 36, 68 and 117-118 of the NISM Series-I workbook support the options-versus-futures hedging distinction used here.
